overview: This is Polzeath’s main beach (maps call the bay Hayle Bay): a wide, flat stretch of sand right in front of the village, about 460 metres across, that runs a long way out at low tide. Most of it disappears under the sea at high water, so the size of your beach depends on the tide.

Polzeath is a lively little surfing village about ten kilometres north-west of Wadebridge, with shops, cafés and pubs along the seafront. It’s one of the busiest beaches on this bit of coast in summer, and has a fun, bustling feel.

expect.title: Surf
expect.text: The RNLI describes the surf here as good quality, and with some shelter from the wind the bay is full of surfers of all kinds in summer.

expect.title: Wildlife
expect.text: Dolphins are sometimes spotted in the bay, and the cliffs to the north are good for birdwatching, with puffins occasionally nesting on the offshore islands.

expect.title: Pentireglaze
expect.text: At the northern end, a smaller beach locals call Baby Bay is cut off from the main beach by a rocky point at high tide.

goodToKnow.label: Tides
goodToKnow.text: The beach shrinks a lot at high tide, and on the biggest spring tides the sea can even flood the seafront car park.

goodToKnow.label: Coast path
goodToKnow.text: The coast path runs through the village, south to Daymer Bay and north out to Pentire Head.

week.text: Go when the tide’s low to mid for the most sand. Polzeath makes an easy beach day with everything on hand, and the walk out to Pentire Head is a great way to stretch your legs afterwards.

pairWith.why: the smaller cove just to the north
a quieter beach towards Daymer Bay
across the estuary for harbour, food and boat trips

tips: Check the tide times: at high tide there’s very little beach left.
In summer, arrive early to get a parking space near the front.
